storage.binding_hint: Chosen from the stores this deployment has.
storage.binding_next: This decides where the NEXT archived original goes. It moves nothing already written: what is under _assets/ stays there.
storage.binding_sub: A name, committed to _meta/ so it travels in a snapshot — never an endpoint and never a credential.
storage.endpoint_hint: Empty means the provider's own public endpoint.
storage.env_note: A store declared by the environment is reinstated at every restart, so it is read here and withdrawn there.
storage.key_hint: Stored write-only: no listing, no response and no audit row ever carries it back.
storage.key_keep: Leave blank to keep the stored credential.
storage.key_pair: An access key and a secret are one identity: send both, or neither.
storage.name: Name
storage.name_hint: How a forest binds it. Fixed once the store exists.
storage.none: No store configured. Originals stay in the forest, under the branch's _assets/.
storage.path_style_hint: MinIO and most self-hosted gateways need it; AWS does not.
storage.prefix_hint: Optional path inside the bucket. Every forest gets its own folder under it.
storage.probe_left: The probe object is still there, at {key} — this credential could write it and not remove it.
storage.reach_read_hint: A store serves every forest and its credential pays for every forest, so changing one asks for admin over all of them. You may read the list and bind this forest to a name.
storage.remove_hint: Removing a store removes no binding and no byte: a forest that named it simply stops having it, and the objects in the bucket are untouched.
storage.stores_sub: Where this deployment can keep the original a converted document was made from.
storage.unmet: This forest expects a store named {name} and this deployment does not have one. Nothing fails: the next original is kept here instead, and the batch report says so.
